findings.title: Negative offsets are passed straight into a Django queryset slice
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled, a client-controlled negative `cursor.offset` is used directly as `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django querysets raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported") for negative slice bounds, so any such cursor produces a 500 error. The comment claiming the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" is wrong, and the stated purpose of reaching data "beyond normal pagination bounds" is a red flag for this feature.

findings.title: BasePaginator still slices with a negative offset for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps the offset only for forward cursors. A user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `0:-5:1`) still reaches `queryset[-5:...]`, which makes Django raise and the request return a 500. This path is shared by every endpoint that uses Paginator or DateTimePaginator. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError` instead.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the attribute, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises a `TypeError`. The cursor value would also be compared as a raw integer against a datetime column. The optimized path is therefore broken for its only caller.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.body: For a superuser who is not a member of the organization, `organization_context.member` can be None. Because `or` short-circuits, superusers happen to be safe. However, a non-superuser request reaching this line with no membership would raise `AttributeError` on `.has_global_access`. Guard the member lookup explicitly instead of relying on evaluation order.

findings.title: Span eviction is silent and the cap is hardcoded
findings.body: Segments larger than 1000 spans are now trimmed with `zpopmin`, which drops the spans with the earliest end timestamps, possibly including the root span. No metric or log records this, whereas the removed Python check emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded`. The limit is also hardcoded in the script, so `max_segment_spans` in `SpansBuffer` is now unused. No test covers the eviction behaviour.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without explanation
findings.body: The loop bound for following redirects drops from 10000 to 1000, and the comment noting that deeper segment trees may not be joined correctly was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now be split incorrectly, and the PR gives no justification for the change.

findings.title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl into the wrong positional slot
findings.body: `__reduce__` passes `redis_ttl` as the fourth positional argument, which the constructor binds to `segment_page_size`. After pickling to multiprocessing workers, the buffer ends up with the wrong page size and the default TTL. This bug predates the PR, but the PR is touching the related segment configuration.
